bet.text: Load from any angle: the turret stays pointed at the goal the entire match, so the robot can intake a note, come back and shoot immediately.

demand.text: At the reveal, a reply that reads as the team's says the robot scored in the speaker, that its amp and climb plans had unresolved issues and would come at later events, and that no trap function was designed in unless shooting from the ground worked.

cycle.text: The under-bumper intake takes a note, four rollers on the turret pull it to the center at any turret angle, and the shooter takes it up with the turret already aimed. The robot also passes notes, added as another superstructure state.

endgame.text: A light, simple climber, done at the end of the season, uses a worm gear to prevent back drive.

fallback.text: When no speaker tag is in view, the code aims the turret from the robot's pose, which is reset from the field tags the camera sees.

gave_up.text: Posters weighing 254's Newton pick say it could not score the trap, its amp was slower and less certain, and its championship auto was not adaptive; others call it the better passer.

A post in 254's voice, which calls it probably the best passer at its best, cites issues in qualifications, little stick time on a fully realized robot, and what 294's defense did to it in Newton match 11.

changed.text: A reply that reads as the team's says a new shooter added an amp mechanism and was more accurate, longer-ranged and nearly 10 pounds lighter.
The climber came at the end of the season.
A post that reads as the team's says two identical robots were intended; the second was never more than a partial chassis because the team was behind schedule.

outcome.text: 50-16-1 in official play; ranked 4 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 58.71, Newton).

solves.text: Make room for the note to enter without making the robot taller

facts.text: Narrow swerve modules from SDS; their standoffs form part of the cage that guides the note
A reply that reads as the team's says it is modeled after the Spectrum intake and takes notes from all kinds of angles
Rollers use black silicone from McMaster, per a reply that reads as the team's
A post that reads as the team's says electrical tape over the silicone of the rearmost intake roller, for less grip at the same thickness, stopped notes escaping out the top
The same post says Teflon tape on the surface opposite the rollers helps notes slide

cost.text: A post that reads as the team's says getting the note through the S-bend draws significant power
The same post says the rollers were wiped with baby wipes before every match to keep their grip

functions.name: Load-from-any-angle feed

solves.text: Feed the shooter whatever direction the turret is pointing

functions.type: four vertical rollers on the turret

facts.text: A note that touches the rollers at any angle is pulled around the turret and to the center, then taken up by the shooter
A reply that reads as the team's likens it to the 254 spindexer with two entry points, so the note enters through the 180-degree arc facing the intake
The side of the turret that receives the note switches as the shooter passes 90 degrees, per a post that reads as the team's

cost.text: Feeding takes slightly longer with the turret at 90 or 270 degrees, because the 'teacup' rollers touch the note as it enters, per a reply that reads as the team's

solves.text: Be aimed before the robot arrives, with the stage or other robots in the way

facts.text: Range either side of center, per a reply that reads as the team's
Tracks the speaker continuously in teleop
Shooting spins up the flywheels, feeds the note and points the turret at the goal
A later version was nearly 10 pounds lighter with greater range and accuracy, per a reply that reads as the team's

solves.text: Score the amp with the shooter without the note falling back out

facts.text: The shooter fires the note straight up and the bar keeps it from falling out
The team says the amp part had to be light
Light and simple, with a worm gear to prevent back drive

cost.text: A post that reads as the team's says the design put high load on the climber motor: it stalled after early successes, then drew about 180 amps after a firmware rollback; one motor burned out at the district championship even though the team e-stopped right after climbing. No root cause was found and other designs are recommended

solves.text: Keep the turret on the goal when the tag is hidden

facts.text: With a speaker tag in view, the turret set point is moved to drive the horizontal error to zero
Without one, the robot's pose gives a field-relative turret angle, converted to robot-relative from the drive heading
Field tags reset odometry, with the robot pose calculated for where the rotating camera sits

cost.text: A camera that rotates on the turret made the pose calculation a problem the team had to work through

solves.text: Avoid several interdependent commands per button

facts.text: A button pushes one super-state, and the superstructure pushes sub-states to each subsystem
The class extends the WPILib subsystem base, so it makes state transitions periodically
Height with the shooter down, about, per a reply that reads as the team's
The reveal post calls it the team's shortest robot yet

decisions.choice: Prototype the roller feed before designing the robot
decisions.because: the team did not know whether rollers at the center could pull a note to the middle

decisions.choice: One superstructure class that pushes states
decisions.because: it keeps the code clean and makes features such as passing easy to add
decisions.instead_of: buttons that each run several interdependent commands

decisions.choice: Use the shooter and a light bar for the amp
decisions.because: the amp part had to be light

decisions.choice: Worm gear on a light, simple climber
decisions.because: the climber was done at the end of the season and had to resist back drive
